akari.title: The Umbrella
akari.text:
Akari finds you on a bench in the afternoon crush of the market street. She sits down next to you with the umbrella folded across her lap. The sky is cloudless and has no use for it.

She's quiet, which isn't like her. She picks at the umbrella's strap.

"I was a few steps behind you two. At the crossing." She says it quickly. "Just walking by. I had this in my bag, and a pack of those sour candies you like. I was going to catch up and pretend it was an accident."

She digs in her pocket and shows you. The packet is still sealed. It's gone soft at the corners from being carried.

"Kenta stopped to tie his shoe," she says, in a smaller voice. "He was way back. He's fine. He's definitely fine. He's probably eaten everything in my fridge by now."

Her smile is very bright and her eyes aren't. She looks at you as if she's daring you to say otherwise.
ngpp: She's snapping the umbrella strap open and shut when she stops and looks down at the bench slats. She runs a thumbnail along the grain. "Weird," she says, "I feel like I've gripped this exact splintery plank before. Next to you." She laughs it off, a little too fast.

"I remember every afternoon walking home behind you and Kenta," Akari says, blinking down the street. "Every one. So why does sitting on this bench feel like I've done it in a different life? With the same sour candies?" She holds the packet tighter.

She drops her forehead against your sleeve without teasing first. "Earth makes sense in my head, Sam," she says. "And the part of me I can't explain remembers leaning on your shoulder, right here, on this bench. I know it did. I'm not making it up."

choices.label: "He's fine. He's the luckiest guy I know."
choices.res: "He's fine. He's the luckiest guy I know," you say. Something in her shoulders unlocks. She leans against your arm, and for a whole minute the loudest girl in the market doesn't make a single joke, which is a personal record. "Thanks for not saying it was nothing," she mumbles. She keeps the packet in her fist and doesn't offer you one.

choices.label: Keep it light, just nod along
choices.res: You nod along and keep it light. "Yeah," she says, relieved and a little disappointed, and snaps the umbrella open under the clear sky just to have something to do with her hands. "Obviously. Totally fine." She holds it over both of you for a minute, in full sun, and neither of you mentions it.

image.comp: sitting beside him holding a folded umbrella in her lap, a brave bright smile with worried eyes

akari.title: What a Coincidence
akari.text:
Steam rolls out when you push open the washroom door. Akari is in the tub.

She has her chin propped on her folded arms on the rim. The bubbles are piled up around her with some care. There's a single rubber duck, and it has been placed. Her fingertips are wrinkled, so she has been in here waiting for a good while.

She gasps. One hand flutters up to her mouth. You've seen better acting at a school festival.

"Oh no. Sam. You've caught me in the bath. What a coincidence."

The duck bobs between you. It doesn't look convinced.

She holds the pose. She has clearly planned what happens next, and she's waiting for your line. A patch of bubbles slides slowly off her shoulder, and she moves a little to stop it, and then she isn't quite sure whether she meant to.

1.title: Bubble Timing
1.text:
You step into the steam, and Akari is peeking at you over a mountain of scented foam. Her cheeks are bright pink.

She skips the fake gasp this time. She flicks a handful of bubbles onto your sleeve.

"Took you long enough, Sam. I've been in here so long I've gone wrinkly." She sits up a little, so that her wet shoulders and the tops of her tits come out of the foam, and she watches to see whether you look. You do, and she grins. "Come and wash my back? I can't reach. It's a matter of dramatic necessity."

choices.label: Kneel beside the rim and scrub her shoulders slowly
choices.res: She sits up in the foam to watch you work, and then she can't. You kneel by the rim, take the sponge and start on her shoulders. Her stage bravado goes the second your soapy hands slide down her bare spine. She turns sharply on her knees in the suds, catches your collar and pulls you down toward her wet mouth.
choices.fallbackRes: She chatters at half her usual speed while your knuckles work the knots out of her shoulders. By the end she's stopped talking altogether and is just leaning back against your chest, with her eyes shut and her cheeks pink. "That's not in the script," she says, very quietly. "Don't stop yet. Please."

choices.label: Flick foam back at her and step out grinning
choices.res: You scoop up a handful of foam, throw it at her face and step back out of the steam, grinning. "Hey! Unfair counterattack!" she squeaks, through the door and a mouthful of bubbles. You hear her splash and giggle, and then a pause. Then, much more quietly, she says, "Rematch. Tomorrow. I'll be ready."

image.comp: sitting up in a foam-filled bath, wet shoulders out of the bubbles, flicking foam at him, sly grin, pink cheeks

3.title: Improvised Script
3.text:
Steam curls around bare skin when you open the door. Akari isn't hiding behind any bubbles tonight.

She's sitting up in the hot water, naked, with her wet hair stuck to her collarbone and her nipples hard in the cooler air. She kicks the rubber duck over the side onto the mat. Then she reaches out with both hands and gets hold of the front of your hoodie.

"No acting tonight, Sam. I'm done with the script." She pulls. "Bolt the latch and get in here with me. I've been wet for you since lunch, and I'm tired of pretending it's the bath."

choices.label: Drop your clothes and climb straight into the tub with her
choices.res: You drop your clothes on the mat, and she watches every piece go. "There he is," she says. You climb in, and the water slops over the rim onto the cedar boards. Akari grabs your shoulders and pulls you down against her, her wet tits against your chest and her mouth hot on your neck.

choices.label: Slide behind her and touch her slowly under the water
choices.res: You slide in behind her, and she melts back against your bare chest, pushing her wet hair aside for you. Her breath catches against your jaw. Your hands come around her waist and rest there, low, under the surface, while she talks too fast about nothing. "Okay," she says, and her voice drops. "Okay, I'm not talking anymore."

image.comp: sitting up in hot water, wet hair stuck to collarbone, hard nipples, rubber duck kicked aside, pulling him by the front of his hoodie, eager look

choices.label: Back out and close the door
choices.res: You back out and close the door. "Coward!" she yells after you, over the squeak of a furious duck. The door shuts on her cackling, and you can hear her sulking happily for a full minute afterward. Then the water sloshes, and she calls, "I'll leave the duck out for you tomorrow. Think about what you did."

choices.label: "You're Kenta's sister."
choices.res: "You're Kenta's sister." A sponge hits the door as it closes. "I KNOW whose sister I am!" You stand in the corridor, and a minute later you hear her, from inside, much quieter, with the water barely stirring. "I'm tired of only being that." You don't know whether she meant you to hear it, and you don't go back in.

choices.label: Burst out laughing
choices.res: You burst out laughing, and she tries to stay offended, lips pressed flat and eyebrows drawn down. It lasts four seconds. Then she slides under the bubbles and comes up laughing so hard the water slops onto the floor. "You're supposed to say my line," she wheezes. "What was my line?" She never did write down your part.

image.comp: lounging in a bath, obviously waiting, fake-gasping with a hand over her mouth

akari.title: Game Night
akari.text:
Akari organizes a staff game night in the lounge. It's a card game she half remembers from Kenta's apartment. She invents the other half as she goes and shouts the new rules over the clinking of mugs.

Nobody understands it. Everybody is having a good time.

She wins. She wins loudly, and there's a victory dance with pointing.

Halfway through the next round she stops in the middle of a cheer.

She has just watched you do it. You held a card a moment too long, then set it down where she could take it. Now she's thinking back, and she can see you've been doing that for an hour.

The table goes a little blurry for her.

"You always did that," she says, very quietly, under the noise. "At Kenta's. Every game night. I'd win, and he'd complain, and you'd say I was just good at it." She looks at the cards in her hand. "I thought I was imagining it. I thought I was making it up because I wanted it to be true."

choices.label: Claim your winner's prize after everyone goes upstairs
choices.res: The last mug goes upstairs, and Akari shoves the scattered cards across the sofa cushions. She grabs you by the front of the hoodie and pulls you down onto the sofa with her, breathless and flushed, knocking cards onto the floor. "I waited six whole years to collect on that cheat," she whispers against your ear. "So. Collect."

choices.label: Stay with her after the others drift off
choices.res: When the others have gone she gathers the cards into a clumsy stack and bumps her shoulder against yours. "Teach me to cheat properly," she says, "and I'll let you win once." You show her how to hold a card back. She's terrible at it. The lamp burns lower, and neither of you reaches to turn it up.

choices.label: Keep the mood light and deal another hand
choices.res: "Rematch," she announces, and shuffles so badly that cards spray over the floor. She laughs it off and goes down on her knees to pick them up. You see her sneak a look at you from under the table, a second longer than the joke needs, with a colour in her cheeks that isn't from the wine.

image.comp: holding a hand of cards up to her face, peeking over them at him with a stunned, delighted grin
image.setting: inn lounge, staff gathered around a table, lamplight

akari.title: Useless
akari.text:
A client complains about Akari in front of half the common room. He does it loudly. She spilled his wine when she poured it, and she talked through his whole evening, and he wants to know what he's paying for.

She laughs it off and apologizes and comps the bottle. She's bright and bouncy until he leaves.

An hour later you hear a sniffle from behind the linen closet door.

She's sitting on a stack of folded sheets in the dark, with a towel clutched against her chest. Her mascara has run.

"I'm useless," she says. "I keep doing the voice and the smile, and it's all I've got. I'm the one who tagged along behind you and Kenta carrying the snacks. That's who I was back home, and I came all the way to another world, and I'm still that."

She wipes her eyes on the towel, which makes it worse.

"I wanted to be somebody you'd notice. I thought it'd be easier here."
ngpp: She's reaching for your sleeve when she stops. Her hand hovers over the stack of sheets, and her eyes unfocus a little. "Huh," she says, sniffling. "I know how soft this is. I know it before I touch it." She shakes her head and takes your sleeve anyway.

"Why does this closet smell safe before you even open the door, Sam?" she sniffles against your hoodie. "I knew you'd come. Not hoped. Knew." She pulls back and stares at the shelves, her mascara in streaks. "Is that a thing I'm allowed to know?"

Akari pulls you down beside her onto the sheets without bothering to hide her tears. "I remember every stupid snack run back in Tokyo, Sam," she says. "And the part I can't remember still knows you never walk past this door without sitting down. Don't argue. I'm sure."

choices.label: "You don't have to do this. You can quit."
choices.res: "That's not what I wanted you to say." She doesn't come out of the closet for an hour. When she does, the linens are folded with furious, perfect corners, and she works the floor without a word and without a single joke. She does it so well that you realise how much you've asked of her, and you don't know how to take it back.

choices.label: Train her yourself, every evening
choices.res: Every evening for a week, after close, you walk her through it, patient and bad at demonstrating. She's clumsy for three days. She drops things, laughs in the wrong places and cries once into a pillow. On the fourth day it clicks. She gets better, then a lot better, and by the end of the week she's showing off.

choices.label: Tell her about your own failures
choices.res: You tell her about the truck, about the three jobs you failed to keep, about the time you cried in a convenience store over a vending machine that ate your last coin. By the end she's laughing through her tears and hitting you with a towel. "You told Kenta none of that," she says. "Did you?" You didn't.

image.comp: crying in a linen closet hugging a stack of towels
image.setting: cramped linen closet, a sliver of light

akari.title: Drama Date
akari.text:
Akari wants a proper date, like in the dramas, and she has storyboarded it. There are drawings. You're a stick figure with a hood.

Scene one is a shared umbrella in the rain. Scene two is a dramatic run to the station. There's no station in Hollowmere, so she's substituted the fountain. Scene three is a long, meaningful look under a streetlamp.

The rain turns up on schedule. She finds that suspicious and squints at the sky.

You do the umbrella. You do the run, and she shouts the directions.

Under the streetlamp she takes up her position and tilts her face to you, and then the whole thing falls apart. The umbrella droops in her fist. Her hair is plastered to her cheek.

"I've rehearsed this in my head for years," she says. "On the train, in the bath. I know every line of it." Her lip wobbles. "I'm terrible at the real thing. I don't know where to put my hands. You're really here, and I don't know my part."

choices.label: Commit to every drama cliche
choices.res: You hold the umbrella high, gaze meaningfully into the rain, and at the end of the sentence you trip into her arms on purpose, with an actor's gasp. She nearly dies of happiness, and then of laughing. "Cut! Do it again!" she squeals. You do it again, worse, and she films it in her head, with her face pressed against your shoulder.

choices.label: Do it your own way
choices.res: You skip the script. A walk in the drizzle, warm buns from the bakery, a quiet bench under the eaves where you share the last one. She goes quiet in the middle of a bite. "Okay," she admits, and leans against you, her hair damp on your collar. "This is better than the dramas. Don't tell the dramas."

image.comp: running dramatically through the rain toward him holding an umbrella

akari.title: Not Kenta's Sister
akari.text:
You're on the roof, hiding from the paperwork, when the ladder creaks. Akari climbs up with a lantern in one hand. The evening wind has pulled her hair loose and the star clip is hanging on by one tooth.

She sits down across from you. Then she stands up again. She can't keep still.

"Okay. I'm going to say this, and you're not going to make a joke."

She puts the lantern down.

"I've had a crush on you since I was sixteen, Sam. It was the haircut, and the bad boss, and all of it. Everybody knew. Kenta knew. I think you knew, and you were too nice to say so." She pushes her hair out of her face. "I'm done keeping it to myself. I'm not Kenta's sister up here. I'm a grown woman, I know what I want, and it's you."

Her voice cracks on the last word. She doesn't look away.

This time you don't climb down.
ngpp: She's holding the lantern high against the evening wind when she stops. Her fingers run over the rim, and she frowns. "I know this is going to sound strange," she says. "But I think I've stood on this roof and yelled this at you already. I can almost hear it."

"Why does standing on these roof tiles feel like I rehearsed it?" Akari laughs wetly, gripping your collar. "Not in a bath, Sam. Here. I know where the wind comes from. I know where to put my feet. Is there something wrong with me?" She doesn't wait for the answer.

"Reset the world a hundred times, Sam," she says, with the lantern at her feet. "I remember every Tokyo summer, and I remember the roof, and the speech. I've said all of this before, and I'll climb up here again every time. So stop looking so stunned and say something."
akari.goLead: Akari sets the lantern down by the chimney, where it's safe, and throws herself into your arms. She kisses you until she's out of breath, and then she pulls you toward the attic hatch and your bed.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.res: Akari nods, brave and bright and a little crushed. "I can wait," she says, tapping the lantern, and her voice only shakes at the end. "Don't make me wait longer than a drama season, okay?" She picks up the lantern, climbs back down the ladder, and from halfway down you hear her whisper, "Okay. Okay."
